paper.title: No-Regret Online Autobidding Algorithms in First-price Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: Online bidding in repeated first-price auctions with ROI constraint, known competing bid distribution
unmapped: Bids in [0,1] in a first-price auction; values v_t i.i.d. from unknown distribution H observed before bidding (acts as a context)
Long-term ROI constraint (total payment <= total value) with ROI violation measured as a second performance metric
Learner knows the competing-bid CDF F exactly
Benchmark is the optimal (possibly randomized) bidding strategy in hindsight knowing F and the value sequence
settings.definition_quote: In this subsection, we describe a no-regret online bidding algorithm (see \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_under_F}) when the competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ is known to the bidder, while the value distribution $\valDist$ still remains unknown.

settings.name_in_paper: Online autobidding in first-price auctions with ROI constraint, full feedback
unmapped: Bids in [0,1] in a first-price auction; competing bid d_t i.i.d. from unknown F; values i.i.d. from unknown H observed before bidding
Full feedback = the maximum competing bid d_t is observed after each round
Long-term ROI constraint with ROI violation as second metric
Benchmark is optimal randomized bidding strategy in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: Full feedback: At the end of round $t$, the bidder observes the competing bid $d_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online autobidding in first-price auctions with ROI constraint, bandit (one-bit) feedback
unmapped: Bids in [0,1] in a first-price auction; competing bid d_t i.i.d. from unknown F; values i.i.d. from unknown H observed before bidding
Bandit feedback = only the binary win indicator 1{d_t <= b_t} is observed
Long-term ROI constraint with ROI violation as second metric
Benchmark is optimal randomized bidding strategy in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: Bandit feedback: At the end of round $t$, the bidder only receives a binary signal $\win_t\in\{0, 1\}$ indicating whether she won the item or not, i.e., $\win_t = \indicator{\competingbid_t \le \bid_t}$.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1: No-regret bidding algorithm for known F (dual mirror descent on F_conv)
Algorithm 2: No-regret bidding algorithm with full feedback (doubling-stage restarts with optimistic empirical CDF)
Algorithm 3: No-regret bidding algorithm with bandit feedback (explore-then-exploit with conservative optimistic CDF)

conditions: competing bid distribution F known to the learner

source.label: prop:performance algo known F
source.quote: For any unknown value distribution $\valDist$, the expected regret of \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_under_F} under any competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ is bounded by $\TotalRegret(\text{\Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_under_F}} \mid (\CDF, \valDist)) = O(\sqrt{T})$, and the expected ROI violation is bounded by ... $\le 2\log T \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Regret defined as expected (over values) difference between reward of optimal randomized strategy in hindsight and the algorithm, with allocation F(b) in expectation; mapped to pseudo_regret with best_policy comparator.

conditions: competing bid distribution F known to the learner

source.label: prop:performance algo known F
source.quote: the expected ROI violation is bounded by $\TotalROIViolation(\text{\Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_under_F}} \mid (\CDF, \valDist)) \le 2\log T \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Expected ROI violation (total payment minus total value).

source.label: thm:randomized_algorithm_full_feedback
source.quote: For any unknown competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ and unknown value distribution $\valDist$, under the setting with full feedback, the expected regret of \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy} is bounded by $\TotalRegret(\mathrm{\Cref{alg:randomized_strategy}} \mid (\CDF, \valDist)) = \widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$, and the expected ROI violation is bounded by ... $= \widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Benchmark: optimal randomized strategy in hindsight.

source.label: thm:randomized_algorithm_full_feedback
source.quote: and the expected ROI violation is bounded by $\TotalROIViolation(\mathrm{\Cref{alg:randomized_strategy}} \mid (\CDF, \valDist)) = \widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Expected ROI violation; Lemma B.6 gives O(sqrt(T) log T) for fixed value sequence.

tuning: M = Theta(sqrt(T)) exploration rounds per grid point

source.label: thm:bandit_feedback-regret_ros
source.quote: For any unknown competing bid distribution $\competingbidDist$ and unknown value distribution $\valDist$, under the bandit feedback, the expected regret of \Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_with_bandit_feedback} with $M = \Theta(\sqrt{T}), K = \Theta(T^{1/4})$ is bounded by ... $= \widetilde O(T^{3/4})$, and the expected ROI violation is bounded by ... $= \widetilde O(T^{3/4})$.

results.notes: Paper's K is number of discretization intervals, not arms; here it's an algorithm parameter.

source.label: thm:bandit_feedback-regret_ros
source.quote: and the expected ROI violation is bounded by $\TotalROIViolation(\mathrm{\Cref{alg:randomized_strategy_with_bandit_feedback}} \mid (\CDF, \valDist)) = \widetilde O(T^{3/4})$.
